primitives.name: Binary Kinship Encoding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each kinsman can be described in two ways, either by letters or by a number.
primitives.assumptions: Kinship relationships are deterministic and fully observed. No missing data or misclassification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Applicable only to complete family trees with known parentage.

layer2.mapping: Maps kinship lineage to binary arithmetic, enabling probabilistic Bayesian network construction for genetic inheritance patterns.
layer2.telemetry: Observed deviations in Mendelian inheritance ratios serve as empirical verification metrics.

primitives.name: p0266 Operator 2
primitives.verbatim_quote: In ordinary cases both the letter and number are intended to be used simultaneously, thus FF.8.
primitives.assumptions: Parental designation follows strict alphabetical convention (F/M) without ambiguity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Valid only for biparental families with clear generational progression.

layer2.mapping: Dual alphabetic-binary representation enables conformal prediction intervals for ancestral state reconstruction.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency checks between letter-based and numeric-based lineage assignments detect database errors.

primitives.name: p0266 Operator 3
primitives.verbatim_quote: The "subject" of the pedigree is of generation O; that of his parents, of generation 1'; that of his grandparents, of generation 2, &c.
primitives.assumptions: Generational counting starts from the proband (O) and increments by one per parental generation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Applicable to finite, non-cyclical pedigrees with known root individual.

layer2.mapping: Generational order forms the basis for hierarchical Bayesian models of trait transmission across discrete time steps.
layer2.telemetry: Mean number of generations traced serves as a proxy for sampling completeness in epidemiological studies.
